info.name: Sprint 7 — Trade API + Fauxnance + Kafka Duplicate-Delivery Demo
info.description:
Covers every real HTTP surface in this sprint (trade-api, and the live Fauxnance sandbox), plus the Kafka duplicate-delivery demo (SEC4-616) documented as runnable steps.

**Important — read before running:**

1. **The Trade Executor has no HTTP API at all.** It's a background worker (Kafka consumer + producer + JDBC client + outbound HTTP client to Fauxnance) — it never listens on a port, so there is nothing for Postman to call directly. The "Trade Executor (no HTTP surface)" folder documents how to check on it instead (process check, consumer-group lag, log tail).
2. **Kafka has no native Postman request type used here.** The "Kafka — Duplicate Delivery Demo" folder's items are placeholders (a harmless GET to trade-api's health endpoint) whose real content is in each item's Description tab — copy the shell command from there into a terminal. This keeps the collection valid/importable everywhere rather than relying on Postman's newer, less portable Kafka request type.
3. **Stack must already be running** per `design/local-demo-runbook.md` — Postgres, Kafka (with topics created), trade-api, and the executor process, all locally.
4. **Fauxnance's mock data is US-equity only.** The demo seed's own instruments (`TCS`, `INFY`) are NOT in it — use `AAPL` (already wired into this collection's `{{symbol}}` variable) for anything that needs to actually fill. If `AAPL` isn't in your local `instruments` table yet, run the INSERT in `design/local-demo-runbook.md` step 6, Option B first.
5. **No token-minting script needed** — this collection's pre-request script mints a fresh HS256 JWT automatically before every request, from the `jwtSecret`/`jwtIssuer`/`accountId` collection variables (must match your `.env`). Nothing to run separately.

variable.description: Informational only — referenced in the Kafka folder's step descriptions.

item.name: Trade API
item.description: sprint-06-trade-api, port 8085. Every endpoint OrderController/AccountController expose, plus the actuator health check.

item.name: Place Order — fillable BUY (AAPL, limit above ask)

request.description:
Returns immediately with status NEW — the fill/reject decision happens asynchronously in the executor, a few hundred ms later (it polls Kafka every 500ms). Re-run 'Get order history' after a moment to see it resolve.

Uses `{{$guid}}` as the idempotency key so every run is naturally unique — this request will never itself trigger the ORD-409 duplicate case (see the dedicated request below for that).

Only succeeds while the order is still NEW (ORD-409 once the executor has already settled it — this is the guarded transition, same idea as the executor's own guard 1). {{orderId}} is captured automatically by 'Place Order' above, or set it by hand from an order you already know is still NEW.

query.description: One of NEW, FILLED, CANCELLED, REJECTED — optional.

item.name: Trade API — error catalogue examples
item.description: One request per entry in GlobalExceptionHandler.java's error envelope — {"errorCode":..., "message":...}. Each is set up to deliberately trigger that specific error.

request.description: price and idempotencyKey both missing — 422 VAL-422.

Seed account ACC-10002 (accountId 2) is SUSPENDED — 403 ACC-403. Note this token was minted for {{accountId}} (default 1); AccountAccessDeniedException (also ACC-403) is what you get if the token's own accountId doesn't reach the account you're addressing at all — same code, deliberately, so account keys can't be enumerated by the error response.
100,000 shares at {{price}} vastly exceeds the seed account's cash balance — 400 ORD-400.

item.name: ORD-409 (1/2) — first request with a fixed idempotency key (expect 200)

request.description: Uses the fixed {{dupIdempotencyKey}} (not {{$guid}}) on purpose, so the next request can collide with it. Run this one first.

Identical body to (1/2), same idempotencyKey — the DB's unique constraint on orders.idempotency_key rejects this as 409 ORD-409 'Duplicate order'. Note: if you re-run this whole pair more than once, (1/2) will itself start returning 409 too, since {{dupIdempotencyKey}} is a fixed value — change the collection variable if you need a clean pair again.

item.name: Fauxnance API
item.description: The live external market-data sandbox the executor calls (executor/.../fauxnance/FauxnanceHttpClient.java). Auth is a plain X-Api-Key header, not the JWT used above.

request.description: What ExecutionService calls, once per order, to price it. Response has bid/ask/price — FillRule settles a BUY at ask, a SELL at bid.

item.name: Get batch quotes (what the market-data poller calls)

request.description: Up to 25 symbols per call (MarketDataPoller.MAX_SYMBOLS_PER_REQUEST) — the quota-relevant HTTP request. The poller publishes one Kafka message per symbol from this single response, never one message per batch.
2000 requests/day per key, resets 00:00 UTC. Neither the executor nor the poller currently checks this before calling (per code as written) — this is purely an inspection endpoint for you.

item.name: Trade Executor (no HTTP surface)
item.description:
There is nothing to call here — the executor never binds a listening port. It only makes outbound connections (Kafka consumer + producer, JDBC to Postgres, HTTP to Fauxnance). This folder documents the commands that stand in for 'hitting an endpoint':

**Is it running at all?**
```
jps -l | grep executor.Main
```

**Is it actually connected and consuming (Kafka's view)?**
```
kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server {{kafkaBootstrapServers}} --describe --group trade-executor
```
A live instance shows a real CONSUMER-ID/HOST; "no active members" means it's not connected.

**Is it doing anything (its own output)?**
```
tail -f /tmp/executor.log
```
(wherever you redirected its stdout/stderr when launching it — see design/local-demo-runbook.md step 4).

**What it does per order** — trace: `ExecutionService.execute()` → duplicate check → instrument/account re-checks → `FauxnanceHttpClient.getQuote()` (the Fauxnance API folder's 'Get single quote' request above is literally the same call) → `FillRule.decide()` → `SettlementService.settle()`.

item.name: Kafka — Duplicate Delivery Demo (SEC4-616)
item.description:
Proves a replayed order message does not double-debit the account and does not produce a second trade-events message (design/demo-duplicate-delivery.md, and design/local-demo-runbook.md step 8, run for real).

Postman has no portable, universally-importable request type for raw Kafka produce/consume, so the three Kafka-specific steps below are placeholders — each one's Description tab holds the exact shell command to run in a terminal instead. The balance/position checks around them ARE real requests you can run from Postman.

**Run in this order:**
1. Place an order (Trade API folder) and let it resolve to a terminal status (FILLED or REJECTED) — check via 'Get Order History' until status isn't NEW anymore.
2. 'Step 1 — Capture the ORDER_PLACED message' (placeholder, see its description).
3. 'Step 2 — Balance & position BEFORE replay' (real requests, below).
4. 'Step 3 — Replay the captured message' (placeholder, see its description).
5. 'Step 4 — Balance & position AFTER replay' (real requests, below) — must be identical to step 3's result.
6. 'Step 5 — Confirm exactly one trade-events message' (placeholder, see its description).

item.name: Step 1 — Capture the ORDER_PLACED message [terminal command — see description]
item.description:
This request itself does nothing useful — it's a harmless placeholder so this step has a valid Postman item. Run this in a terminal instead, then paste the matching line into a file (e.g. /tmp/replay-message.txt):

```
docker exec team4se4-kafka-1 /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-console-consumer.sh \
  --bootstrap-server {{kafkaBootstrapServers}} \
  --topic orders --from-beginning --property print.key=true --timeout-ms 6000 \
  | grep "<the order's public UUID — from {{orderId}}, or the Place Order response>"
```

Save the matching `<key>\t<json value>` line, preserving the tab, to a file for step 3.

item.name: Step 3 — Replay the captured message [terminal command — see description]
item.description:
Placeholder — run this in a terminal, preserving the key exactly (the file from step 1, formatted as `<key>:<value>` on one line):

```
docker exec -i team4se4-kafka-1 /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-console-producer.sh \
  --bootstrap-server {{kafkaBootstrapServers}} \
  --topic orders --property "parse.key=true" --property "key.separator=:" \
  < /tmp/replay-message.txt
```

Wait a few seconds for the executor to pick it up (it polls every 500ms) before running step 4.

item.name: Step 4a — Balance AFTER replay (must match 2a exactly)

exec: console.log('Compare this cashBalance against Step 2a\'s response by hand — they must be identical.');

item.name: Step 4b — Positions AFTER replay (must match 2b exactly)
Step 5 — Confirm exactly one trade-events message [terminal command — see description]
item.description:
Placeholder — run in a terminal:

```
docker exec team4se4-kafka-1 /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-console-consumer.sh \
  --bootstrap-server {{kafkaBootstrapServers}} \
  --topic trade-events --from-beginning --property print.key=true --timeout-ms 6000 \
  | grep '"orderId":<the order's NUMERIC id, not the UUID — check via psql or the executor log>'
```

Exactly one line should match — never two. Also worth grepping the executor's log for the guard-1 dedup line:

```
grep DUPLICATE_DELIVERY /tmp/executor.log
```
Expect exactly one new line after the replay, e.g. `DUPLICATE_DELIVERY orderId=7 status=FILLED — already processed, skipping`.
